definition: An architecture with a retention mechanism admitting three equivalent computation modes: parallel for training, recurrent for O(1) inference, and chunkwise for long sequences.
details: An architecture with a retention mechanism admitting three equivalent computation modes: parallel for training, recurrent for O(1) inference, and chunkwise for long sequences. A landmark in the search for a "transformer successor" with cheaper inference.

explainer.lead: RetNet is an architecture built on a retention mechanism that supports three equivalent computation modes: parallel for training, recurrent for O(1) inference, and chunkwise for long sequences. It is a landmark in the search for a transformer successor with cheaper inference.

tiers.eli5: The same engine can run in three gears: one fast for learning, one cheap for answering one step at a time, and one for handling very long inputs.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train in the parallel mode, then switch to the recurrent mode for constant-cost inference, or use the chunkwise mode for long sequences. A pitfall is assuming the modes differ in results; they are presented as equivalent.
tiers.paperLevel: An architecture with a retention mechanism admitting three equivalent computation modes: parallel for training, recurrent for O(1) inference, and chunkwise for long sequences. O(1) refers to inference cost per step; the definition states no further complexity bounds.

explainer.example: A model is trained with the parallel mode and then served with the recurrent mode so each new token costs constant time.
